chapter.li: LEChapter10 Verse1 This is what Amulek preached to the people in Ammonihah: VerseEnd Verse2 I’m Amulek, the son of Gidanah, the son of Ishmael, a descendant of Aminadi — the same Aminadi who interpreted the writing on the temple wall, written by God’s finger. VerseEnd Verse3 And Aminadi was a descendant of Nephi, the son of Lehi, who came from the land of Jerusalem and was a descendant of Manasseh, the son of Joseph, who was sold into Egypt by his brothers. VerseEnd Verse4 I’m also influential with those who know me. I have many relatives and friends. I’ve become wealthy through hard work. VerseEnd Verse5 Despite all this, I’ve never known much about the Lord’s ways, mysteries, and awe-inspiring power. I said I didn’t know much about these things, but that isn’t completely accurate. I’ve watched His mysterious, miraculous power protecting the lives of this people. VerseEnd Verse6 But I hardened my heart. I had many opportunities to hear Him but refused to listen. Therefore, although I knew God did these things, I refused to acknowledge it. I kept rebelling against God in the wickedness of my heart, up until the fourth day of this seventh month, in the 10th year of the judges’ rule. VerseEnd

Verse7 As I went to see a close relative, an angel of the Lord appeared and said: Amulek, return to 2PSI your own house. There 2PSI you will feed a prophet of the Lord, a holy man who’s a chosen man of God. He’s fasted many days because of the sins of this people, and he’s weakened by hunger. 2PSI You’re to welcome him into 2PSI your house and feed him. He’ll bless 2PSI you and 2PSI your family, and the Lord’s blessing will then be on 2PSI you and 2PSI your family. VerseEnd

Verse8 So I obeyed the angel’s voice and returned to my house. I was on my way and met the man the angel told me to welcome to my house. He is this same man who’s been telling 2PP you about the things of God. VerseEnd Verse9 The angel told me: He is a holy man. I know he’s a holy man because God’s angel said it. VerseEnd Verse10 I also know the things he’s testified about are true. I tell 2PP you as the Lord lives, He absolutely sent His angel to reveal this to me, and He’s blessed my house while this man named Alma has been there. VerseEnd Verse11 Indeed, God has blessed my household: me, the women of my family, my children, my father, and my relatives. God has even blessed all my relatives because we believed what Alma has taught us. VerseEnd

Verse12 Now when Amulek said this, the people were shocked, because there was now more than one witness who condemned them, confirming what was going to happen, based upon the spirit of prophecy in them. VerseEnd Verse13 Nevertheless, some of them were determined to challenge them, trying to trap them in a contradiction. They asked trick questions to find evidence against them. They hoped to hand them over to the judges, intending for them to be judged under the law and be executed or imprisoned for any crime they could accuse them of committing. Or for any crime they could make it appear they had committed. VerseEnd

Verse14 Now their accusers trying to destroy them were lawyers who were hired or appointed to serve the law during their trials — civil and criminal — held before their judges. VerseEnd Verse15 These lawyers would argue artfully and debate deceptively, proving their proficiency in their profession. VerseEnd Verse16 So they began to question Amulek to get him confused, hoping to hear a contradiction. VerseEnd Verse17 Now they didn’t realize Amulek anticipated their evil plans. But when they began to question him, he understood their thoughts and told them: 2PP You wicked and corrupt generation, 2PP you lawyers and hypocrites! 2PP You’re laying the accuser’s foundations by planning traps and snares to entrap God’s holy ones. VerseEnd Verse18 2PP You’re planning to corruptly misrepresent a righteous man. That will provoke God’s wrath upon 2PP you, resulting in this people’s complete destruction. VerseEnd Verse19 Mosiah, who was our last king, when he was about to give up the kingdom, had no one to confer it on. That resulted in this people being governed by our own choices. He was right when he said if the time comes when the people choose iniquity, or the people choose transgression, then they would be overdue for destruction. VerseEnd Verse20 I’m telling 2PP you the Lord is right to condemn 2PP you for 2PP your iniquities; He should warn the people with the message from His angels: Repent! Repent, because the kingdom of heaven approaches. VerseEnd Verse21 Indeed, He should warn 2PP you by the message of His angels: I’m coming to be with My people to implement fairness and justice. VerseEnd Verse22 I tell 2PP you if it weren’t for the prayers of the righteous among 2PP you, 2PP you would be punished right now with complete destruction. It wouldn’t come by a flood, as the people in Noah’s time were killed, but it would be by famine, calamity, disease, and the sword. VerseEnd Verse23 2PP You’re only spared because of the prayers of the righteous. Therefore if 2PP you drive out the righteous from 2PP your community, the Lord won’t hold back His hand, and He’ll confront 2PP you in His fierce anger; and 2PP you’ll be afflicted with famine, calamity, disease, and the sword. That is coming soon unless 2PP you repent. VerseEnd

Verse24 Then the people were even angrier with Amulek, shouting: This man is mocking our laws, that are fair; and our wise lawyers we’ve chosen! VerseEnd Verse25 But Amulek stretched out his hand and thundered back at them, saying: 2PP You wicked and corrupt generation, why has Satan got such firm control on 2PP your hearts? Why do 2PP you choose to submit to him? By trusting him, he is able to rule 2PP you, to blind 2PP your eyes, so 2PP you don’t understand the truth when it’s told to 2PP you. VerseEnd Verse26 I ask: Have I testified against 2PP your law? 2PP You’re confused. 2PP You say I have spoken against 2PP your law, but I haven’t; I’ve defended it, to 2PP your condemnation. VerseEnd Verse27 Now I tell 2PP you the reason this people will be destroyed is because of the unrighteous leadership of 2PP your lawyers and judges. VerseEnd

Verse28 When Amulek said this, the people condemned him: Now we know this man is a child of the accuser, because he’s lied to us and broken our law. But he says he hasn’t broken it. VerseEnd Verse29 He’s denounced our lawyers and judges and others. VerseEnd Verse30 Now it was the lawyers who urged everyone to remember these accusations against him. VerseEnd Verse31 One of them, named Zeezrom, was the most eager one accusing Amulek and Alma. He was one of their best lawyers, in high demand in the community. VerseEnd Verse32 Now the aim of these lawyers was to make money, and they made money by staying busy. VerseEnd
LEChapter11 Verse1 Mosiah’s law paid appointed judges of the law based on the time required of them to decide a matter. VerseEnd

Verse2 If a man owed someone money, but refused to pay his debt, a complaint would be made to the judge. Then the judge would order him to be brought before him, and would send out officers to enforce the order. Then he would judge the man based on the law and evidence against him. So the debtor would be compelled to pay or be whipped, or even expelled from the community as a thief and robber. VerseEnd Verse3 The judge would be paid for the time he worked: being paid a senine of gold for a day, or a senum of silver, which was equal to a senine of gold. This was established by the law. VerseEnd

Verse4 Now these were the names used by the Nephites for the different pieces of their gold and silver, and their values. They didn’t use the same values as the Jews who lived at Jerusalem, nor the same measurements as the Jews either. Instead, they used changing calculations and measurements as people’s choices and circumstances changed every generation till the rule of judges. Then king Mosiah standardized the system of calculations and measurements. VerseEnd

Verse5 Now the calculation was this: a senine, a seon, a shum, and a limnah of gold; VerseEnd Verse6 a senum, an amnor, an ezrum, and an onti of silver. VerseEnd Verse7 A senum of silver was equal to a senine of gold, and each was equal to a measure of barley or any kind of grain. VerseEnd Verse8 Now a seon of gold was twice the value of a senine. VerseEnd Verse9 A shum of gold was twice the value of a seon. VerseEnd Verse10 And a limnah of gold was worth all of them combined. VerseEnd Verse11 An amnor of silver was as valuable as two senums. VerseEnd Verse12 An ezrum of silver was the same value as four senums. VerseEnd Verse13 And an onti was worth all of them combined. VerseEnd Verse14 Now these are the lesser values in their calculation: VerseEnd Verse15 A shiblon was half a senum; so a shiblon equaled half a measure of barley. VerseEnd Verse16 A shilum was half a shiblon. VerseEnd Verse17 And a leah was half a shilum. VerseEnd Verse19 Now an antion of gold was equal to three shiblons. VerseEnd Verse18 These were the quantities used in their calculations. VerseEnd

Verse20 Now the lawyers’ sole objective was to make money, because they received payment according to how much time they spent. They incited people to fight with one another, encouraging disturbances, with resulting wickedness, all so they could have more work, and make money from the resulting lawsuits. This was why they incited people to be angry with Alma and Amulek. VerseEnd Verse21 So Zeezrom started questioning Amulek: If I ask 2PSF you a few questions, will 2PSF you answer them for me? Now Zeezrom was a skilled accuser, serving Satan and opposing righteousness. That was why he asked Amulek: Will 2PSF you answer the questions I ask 2PSF you? VerseEnd Verse22 Amulek replied: Yes, I’ll answer as the Spirit of the Lord inspires me to answer, because I’ll say nothing opposing the Spirit of the Lord. Zeezrom offered to him: Here are six onties of silver; I’ll give all these to 2PSI you if 2PSI you deny a Supreme Being exists. VerseEnd

Verse23 Amulek responded: 2PSI You child of hell, why are 2PSI you trying to trick me? Don’t 2PSI you understand the righteous aren’t tempted by bribes? VerseEnd Verse24 Do 2PSI you really believe there’s no God? I say: No, 2PSI you know there’s a God; but 2PSI you corruptly love money more than Him. VerseEnd Verse25 2PSI You’ve lied before God. 2PSI You made me the offer: I’ll give 2PSI you these six onties — which are very valuable — when 2PSI you actually intended to keep them. 2PSI You just wanted me to deny the true and living God, so 2PSI you could have a reason to execute me. Now because of 2PSI your great evil, 2PSI you’ll have 2PSI your reward. VerseEnd

Verse26 Then Zeezrom asked him: So 2PSI you say there’s a true and living God? VerseEnd Verse27 Amulek replied: Yes, there’s a true and living God. VerseEnd Verse28 Next Zeezrom asked: Is there more than one God? VerseEnd Verse29 He answered: No. VerseEnd Verse30 Zeezrom asked him: How do 2PSI you know these things? VerseEnd Verse31 He said: An angel has revealed them to me. VerseEnd Verse32 Zeezrom then asked: Who’s the one who is to come? Is it the Son of God? VerseEnd Verse33 He answered: Yes. VerseEnd Verse34 And Zeezrom asked again: Will He save His people in their sins? And Amulek answered: I tell 2PSF you that He will not, because it’s impossible for Him to deny His word. VerseEnd

Verse35 Then Zeezrom told the people: See that 2PP you remember these things, because he says on the one hand there’s only one God, but he says on the other hand the Son of God will come but He won’t save His people, as if he had authority to command God. VerseEnd Verse36 Then Amulek rebuked him: 2PSI You have lied! 2PSI You say I speak as if I had authority to command God, because I said He won’t save His people in their sins. VerseEnd Verse37 I repeat that He can’t save them in their sins, because I can’t deny His word. He has said no unclean thing can inherit the kingdom of heaven. So, how can 2PP you be saved unless 2PP you inherit the kingdom of heaven? Therefore 2PP you can’t be saved in 2PP your sins. VerseEnd Verse38 Then Zeezrom asked him: Is the Son of God the very Eternal Father? VerseEnd Verse39 Amulek said to him: Yes, He’s called the very Eternal Father of heaven, earth, and everything that’s in them. He’s the beginning and the end, the first and the last. VerseEnd Verse40 He’ll come into the world to redeem His people. He’ll take upon Himself the transgressions of those who believe in His name; these are the ones who will have eternal life, and salvation isn’t available to anyone else. VerseEnd Verse41 So the wicked remain as if no redemption had been made, except for the chains of death being removed. Indeed, the day will come when all will rise from the dead and stand before God and be judged according to their works. VerseEnd

Verse42 Now there is a mortal death, and Christ’s death will release the chains of this mortal death, so everyone will be raised from this temporal death. VerseEnd Verse43 The spirit and body will be completely restored. Both limb and joint will be restored to their proper form, just like we are now formed; and we’ll be brought to stand before God. We’ll clearly understand right from wrong and truth from error, like we can now. We’ll clearly remember all our guilt. VerseEnd Verse44 Now this restoration will come to all: old and young, enslaved and free, male and female, wicked and righteous. And not so much as a hair of their heads will be missing; but all things will be restored to their perfect form, the same as now, or in the restored body. Then everyone will stand before the judgment seat of Christ the Son, and God the Father, and the Holy Spirit, which collectively are one Eternal God. Then to be judged based on their works, whether they’re good or whether they’re evil. VerseEnd

Verse45 Now I’ve told 2PP you about mortal death and the resurrection of the mortal body. This mortal body will be raised as an immortal body, from that first death back to life. Following that we’ll no longer die, our spirits will unite with our bodies and not be separated again. Through this process, the restoration is spiritual and immortal, and we won’t decay or die again. VerseEnd
Verse46 When Amulek finished saying this, the people were again surprised. Zeezrom began to tremble. That concludes everything I write from Amulek’s talk. VerseEnd
